comparisons.peer_topic: Noninterest expense increase drivers and prior year comparisons
comparisons.peer_summary: Noninterest expense increased $967 million to $66.8 billion in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily driven by higher revenue-related expenses and investments in people, operations, and technology, partially offset by higher FDIC expense in 2023 (including a $2.1 billion special assessment) and lower expenses from a liquidating business activity.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America disclosed that their primary expense increases in 2024 were driven by investments in technology, alongside other operational factors. Citi reported that its transformation-related expenses increased by 1% to $2.9 billion, with the increase 'largely driven by increased spending on certain programs, including data,' which was offset by a reduction in bonus payouts. Similarly, Bank of America reported a total noninterest expense increase of $967 million to $66.8 billion, stating this increase was 'primarily driven by higher revenue-related expenses as well as investments in people, operations and technology.' While Citi's disclosure is specific to transformation costs and includes a specific offset (bonus reduction), Bank of America's broader expense increase also highlights technology investment as a key driver, aligning on the specific business driver of technology spending.

sentences.text: In 2024, Citi's transformation-related expenses increased 1% to approximately $2.9 billion from the prior year, largely driven by increased spending on certain programs, including data, largely offset by a reduction in the payout under the Transformation Bonus Program.

The increase was primarily driven by higher revenue-related expenses as well as investments in people, operations and technology, partially offset by higher Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) expense in 2023, including $2.1 billion for the estimated special assessment amount arising from the closure of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank, and lower expenses related to a liquidating business activity.

comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Morgan Stanley disclosed increases in specific cost categories driven by technology-related spending in 2024. Citi's transformation expenses rose to $2.9 billion, driven by 'increased spending on certain programs, including data.' Morgan Stanley reported that its non-interest expenses increased 5% to $19,129 million, with non-compensation expenses increasing 'primarily reflecting higher execution-related expenses and increased technology spend.' Both disclosures identify technology/data as a primary growth driver for specific expense lines, despite the broader context of Citi's transformation program versus Morgan Stanley's overall operational expenses.
